result:
I'd dissolve the gap between what people actually want and what they think they're supposed to want.

So much suffering seems to come from that friction—people pursuing things that don't genuinely matter to them because of internalized pressure, shame, or scripts they inherited. Then spending decades building a life that doesn't fit.

If people could just *know* what they actually valued without all the noise, I think most other problems would become more tractable. Not solved automatically, but at least people would be working toward things that were real to them. The energy that goes into performance and pretense could go elsewhere.

It's maybe a naive answer—probably the hard part is that people are genuinely confused about what they want, not just prevented from admitting it. But even so.
